_help.about: The biome gate (design 1 Oct §CA, Mike: a species belongs in its natural environment; a savanna is acacias, grass and shrubs). VegetationPlacer placed by climate bands alone, so a floodplain-forest magnolia grew on a savanna riverbank. Now a species grows only in a biome whose file lists it (plants, or an association's dominant / companion / ground / catalogue) and, for a data/plants catalogue entry, only in the biomes its own `biomes` list names. Climate, soil, altitude, needs and the realm gate (§AA) still apply inside those biomes. Restart after editing.
_help.biome_gate: true: the gate is on. false: the old rule (bands only) — for A/B only.
_help.catalogue_needs_biomes: true: a data/plants entry with no `biomes` list does not grow (like an untagged realm) until the fill tags it. false: untagged catalogue entries grow wherever a biome file copies them.
_help.ecotone_m: A neighbouring biome's species may cross the border this far into a biome that does not list them, when their own bands fit. 0: hard borders (Mike, 1 Oct: a gallery forest is a floodplain-forest cell, not a bleed). Open it later if the borders look fake.
_help.association_lists_count: Which lists in a biome's associations count as 'listed' for the gate.
_help.walkabout: tools/walkabout.gd, the end-of-pass check (§CA): seeds, sites per seed, hours, first-person eye height, how far it looks, and that any species in an unlisted biome fails it. Frames and the species list are the report; the dev frame is for grade measurements only.
_help.trim: Design 1 Oct §CC (Mike): the catalogue is trimmed to archetypes. Nine categories (cacti added 12:04); each biome keeps at most per_biome_per_category species per category, and only where the biome has that category at all (a hot desert has no moss; the open ocean has no tree). The most archetypal of what the biome file already lists (the dominant, the companion, the one a flora names first), never a new species. The special catalogues in keep_whole stay as they are. Every other data/plants catalogue file is folded into the biome lists it serves or archived to docs/plant_archive. category_of maps the schema's shape / tier vocabulary onto the eight categories; an entry that fits none (a vine, kelp, a cushion plant, a lichen) is archived unless it is the biome's hero_species. A hero species always survives.

category_of.tree: canopy or emergent tier; shapes broadleaf, conifer, cypress, palm, umbrella (woody); tree ferns go to fern
category_of.shrub: shrub tier, woody; sagebrush, heath, mangrove seedling, bamboo thicket
category_of.grass: grasses, sedges, rushes, reeds, cattail, bamboo grasses; the ground tier's graminoids
category_of.fungi: fungi.json and any ground entry that is a mushroom, bracket, puffball or lichen-as-fungus
category_of.fern: ferns, tree ferns, whisk ferns, selaginella
category_of.aroid: aroids: Alocasia, Colocasia, Philodendron, Monstera, Bucephalandra, skunk cabbage, taro; Amorphophallus stays its own catalogue
category_of.cacti: cacti and the other stem succulents a desert flora groups with them: saguaro, cardon, prickly pear, barrel, cholla, Madagascar ocotillo, euphorbia candelabra; Trichocereus stays its own catalogue
